title: Discovery: Everest Analytics - Embeddings & Reranking
summary: Initial discovery on embeddings + reranking workflow. Customer currently uses FAISS for vector search and is evaluating Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for latency, throughput, and data residency. Key themes: vector DB integration, dimensionality (1536 vs 768), hybrid BM25+embedding rerank, throughput targets (1k qps => 200-400k vectors), security/SOC2 and VPC/KMS requirements, and next step pilot for a 2-week benchmark.
topics: Current stack: FAISS on-prem, Postgres + Elastic for metadata
Embedding model choices and dimensionality (768 vs 1536)
Hybrid search: BM25 + embed rerank vs pure ANN
Vector DB integration options (Pinecone, Milvus, self-hosted FAISS)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (SLA, VPC, KMS)
Security: SOC 2, SAML SSO, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-27 16:00 PT | Duration: 46 min | Attendees: Maya Chen, Jordan Li - Redwood; Priya Sharma, Liam O'Connell, Diego Morales - Everest

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Priya Sharma: Yep all good, thanks Maya. Appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:08] Maya Chen: Awesome, quick intro — I'm Maya AE, Jordan's our solutions engineer. We'll do a discovery to understand your retrieval/rerank flow and then propose hosted vs dedicated vs private options.
[00:18] Jordan Li: Hey, hi all. I'll jump in on latency/throughput technical bits and go over integration patterns.
[00:25] Liam O'Connell: Great, I'm Liam CTO, Priya runs the data team and Diego does the model infra.
[00:31] Diego Morales: hey.
[00:32] Maya Chen: Cool — Priya, could you give a quick picture of current infra and pain points?
[00:36] Priya Sharma: Sure. We run FAISS on k8s clusters in our GCP project. We have ~350k product vectors right now, embeddings at 1536 dims using open models, and we do a hybrid approach — we do BM25 in Elastic for candidate recall, then FAISS ANN to surface top 200 and a rerank model on top (a lightweight cross-encoder) for final ordering. Latency's been creeping up, especially during peak traffic.
[01:06] Jordan Li: when you say latency creeping up, what's the P95 P99 numbers?
[01:10] Priya Sharma: P95 is about 220ms for the full pipeline, P99 ~640ms in spikes. We want P95 under 150ms ideally and P99 under 350ms.
[01:21] Diego Morales: also cost — CPU and GPU infra for reranker is expensive; maintaining FAISS sharding + reindexing adds ops overhead.
[01:30] Maya Chen: That's helpful. Couple clarifying Qs: 1) how many queries per second at peak? 2) are vectors updated frequently?
[01:36] Priya Sharma: Peak qps is about 1k, steady maybe 300. We do nightly bulk updates and a small stream of updates throughout the day (~500 updates/hr).
[01:46] Liam O'Connell: And we have strict data residency for EU customers; some datasets can't leave their region.
[01:52] Jordan Li: Understood. Two main integration paths we see: 1) keep your FAISS self-hosted and use Redwood for hosted embeddings + rerank inference only, or 2) use Redwood's serving + embedding pipeline with Dedicated or Private and migrate vector store to a managed ANN like Pinecone or Milvus — or keep FAISS but run it on Redwood Private. Each has tradeoffs.
[02:14] Diego Morales: If we consider migrating vector store, how do you handle dimensionality differences? We use 1536 now; some LLM embed models are 768. That affects index shape and recall.
[02:24] Jordan Li: good point. We recommend matching embedding dimensionality to your rerank and downstream models. Redwood supports storing arbitrary dim vectors; when you change dims you generally need to reindex. For rerank quality, we've seen 1536 slightly better for semantic nuance but 768 often a good tradeoff for cost. We can run AB evals during pilot.
[02:44] Priya Sharma: AB evals would be great. Also curious about hybrid search latency — our current BM25+ANN+rerank flow adds sequential steps. Can Redwood pipeline reduce that?
[02:55] Jordan Li: yes, two approaches: 1) run BM25 as filter then do ANN on filtered candidates — keeps recall but reduces ANN cost and latency, or 2) dense retrieval only with a stronger embed model to avoid BM25. For most e-comm use cases we recommend hybrid: BM25 for exact matches and embed rerank for semantic results. Redwood Optimize can suggest batch sizes and caching to cut per-token inference cost and improve token throughput for reranker.
[03:20] Liam O'Connell: On throughput — at 1k qps, what footprint do you expect for dedicated?
[03:25] Jordan Li: rough back-of-envelope: with a 1536-d embed, ANN qps depends on index type and hardware. For dedicated serving with GPUs for rerank plus optimized CPU/GPU for ANN, customers at ~1k qps move to a small dedicated pool ~4-8 GPUs plus autoscale for bursts. If you keep FAISS on-prem, Redwood Dedicated can act as the rerank inference plane and call your FAISS endpoints — that reduces migration work.
[03:52] Diego Morales: any numbers on memory per vector? We have 350k * 1536 — memory and index size matter.
[03:58] Jordan Li: depends on index format (IVF, HNSW). HNSW tends to use more memory but lower recall variance. For 1536 dims with float32, raw vectors ~2.1GB for 350k. Index overhead can be multiple times. Quantization (e.g., 8-bit) can reduce size — Redwood supports quantized execution paths and recommends PQ/OPQ for larger catalogs.
[04:22] Priya Sharma: Security — SOC 2, SAML, KMS. We need to know if Redwood Private can live in our VPC and use our KMS.
[04:30] Maya Chen: Yes — Private supports customer-managed VPC and KMS/HSM integration and audit logging. Dedicated has VPC peering options and bring-your-own-key for some tiers, hosted has SOC 2 and encryption at rest but not customer KMS for standard plans. We can share the security pack.
[04:49] Liam O'Connell: And compliance docs — we need SOC 2 report and pen test summary.
[04:52] Maya Chen: We'll send those in the follow-ups.
[04:55] Diego Morales: From an integration standpoint, what connectors do you have for FAISS or vector DBs?
[05:00] Jordan Li: Redwood exposes a standard API for embeddings and rerank. For vector stores we have connectors and recipes for Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, and self-hosted FAISS. For FAISS we typically recommend either running it on your infra and calling it from Redwood, or migrating to a managed vector DB to remove operational overhead. We also provide examples for upsert patterns and incremental reindexing.
[05:23] Priya Sharma: We use internal search service that wraps FAISS — latency's affected by sharding and cross-node calls. Would a Dedicated Redwood node colocated reduce network hops?
[05:34] Jordan Li: yes, Dedicated co-located with your vector store (via VPC peering) reduces latency; Private deployment inside your VPC reduces network hops further.
[05:43] Maya Chen: quick question on SLAs — do you have an internal SLA for ded?
[05:47] Jordan Li: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; hosted has best-effort SLOs. We can provide the SLA doc.
[05:55] Priya Sharma: For the rerank model, do you host the cross-encoder in Redwood or self-host?
[05:59] Jordan Li: both. Many customers host their reranker on Redwood for lower maintenance and autoscaling; others keep it in-house for IP. We can run your reranker as a container on Dedicated or host in Private per your security needs.
[06:12] Diego Morales: If we host rerank here, how do you handle batching and cold-start? We see spikes and want to avoid latency cliffs.
[06:19] Jordan Li: Redwood runtime does continuous batching and adaptive batching thresholds; it also has warm pools to reduce cold-starts. For your 1k qps we would size pools accordingly and test under load in the benchmark.
[06:32] Liam O'Connell: What's a minimal pilot look like?
[06:35] Maya Chen: Typically a 2-week pilot: we run a benchmark with a holdout set, run AB evals on 1536 vs 768 embeddings, test BM25+ANN vs dense retrieval, and measure P95/P99 end-to-end. Pilot includes security review (we'll share SOC2) and an integration guide.
[06:51] Priya Sharma: Timeboxed 2-week pilot sounds good. Who owns infra work?
[06:55] Maya Chen: Redwood supports a faststart: Jordan will help with the integration script and we can provide a small data ingestion recipe. You're responsible for granting access to test data in a sandbox — we don't need production data.
[07:06] Diego Morales: Are there cost-estimates for hosted vs dedicated?
[07:09] Maya Chen: We'll send estimated TCO — hosted per-token + per-embedding pricing, dedicated is a reserved capacity SKU. We'll include an example for 1k qps and 350k vectors with a rerank step.
[07:21] Liam O'Connell: Competitors — we're also talking to Pinecone and Amazon Kendra. Any differentiators?
[07:27] Jordan Li: Redwood differentiator is unified runtime + routing and ability to run same stack across hosted/dedicated/private. So you get consistent performance and rollouts across environments. Also Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization.
[07:42] Priya Sharma: On reindexing — we have nightly builds; can Redwood's connectors support incremental partial upserts to avoid full reindex?
[07:50] Jordan Li: yes, we have upsert patterns and incremental reindex recipes — we'll share a guide.
[07:56] Maya Chen: any regulatory data locality constraints beyond EU?
[07:59] Liam O'Connell: EU only for now.
[08:01] Diego Morales: quick nit — when you say quantized execution, are there quality regressions? We care about ranking quality.
[08:06] Jordan Li: there can be small regressions; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles and run evals against your prompt set to measure delta and pick thresholds where cost savings are worth it.
[08:20] Priya Sharma: Sounds good. A couple of specific asks from our side before pilot: 1) pricing estimate 2) SOC2 and pen test reports 3) integration recipe for FAISS + Redwood 4) sample benchmark plan.
[08:33] Maya Chen: Got it — we'll include those.
[08:36] Liam O'Connell: Also can you share references of customers who migrated from self-hosted FAISS to Redwood Dedicated?
[08:41] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include references — nothing that names customers without approval but anonymized case studies and metrics.
[08:50] Diego Morales: one last technical: how do you handle rerank model latency if we use a large cross-encoder? We need <100ms for rerank ideally.
[08:58] Jordan Li: large cross-encoders can be heavy; for sub-100ms we recommend a distilled cross-encoder or two-stage — a lightweight bi-encoder followed by a small cross-encoder on top N candidates. Redwood's runtime supports model compilers and kernel selection to optimize inference latency.
[09:16] Priya Sharma: ok. Let's recap next steps.
[09:19] Maya Chen: recap: Redwood to send pricing, security docs, FAISS integration recipe, pilot plan and benchmark scripts. Customer to provision sandbox data and confirm pilot cohort. We schedule a technical kick-off next week.
[09:31] Liam O'Connell: works for us.
[09:32] Maya Chen: thanks everyone — Jordan any closing notes?
[09:35] Jordan Li: I'll prepare the technical checklist and a list of metrics we'll capture in the pilot (P95, P99, throughput, recall@k, latency breakdown).
[09:44] Maya Chen: great — we'll follow up with calendar invites. Thanks all.
